This article compares the proportion of atrial fibrillation patients admitted with ischemic stroke or stroke of unknown type who had redeemed a prescription for oral anticoagulation treatment within 100 days prior to their admission. The data is drawn from national and regional healthcare quality reports published in 2024 and 2025, tracking how effectively patients at high risk for stroke were receiving preventative medication before the event occurred.

At the national level, [[danmark|Danmark]] saw a modest improvement in this quality indicator, with the proportion of patients receiving prior anticoagulation therapy rising from 65.5% (739 out of 1128 patients) in the 2024 report [^src1] to 67.3% (772 out of 1147 patients) in the 2025 report [^src2]. 

When examining regional performance, the leadership shifted slightly between the two reporting periods. In the 2024 data, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] was the top-performing region, with 74.3% of its patients having redeemed a prescription prior to admission [^src1]. By the 2025 report, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] took the lead, achieving a 75.4% compliance rate, while Region Syddanmark remained a close second at 73.5% [^src2]. 

Conversely, the lowest-performing regions also changed, highlighting diverging regional trends. [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] recorded the lowest national proportion in the 2024 report at 60.3% [^src1]. However, it demonstrated the most significant positive trend as an outlier, increasing its rate by over seven percentage points to 67.7% in the 2025 report [^src2]. This sharp improvement allowed [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] to become the new trailer; although it started at 61.4% in the earlier report [^src1], it was the only region to experience a notable decline, dropping to 59.1% in the later data [^src2]. Meanwhile, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] maintained relatively stable, mid-tier performance across both periods, moving slightly from 63.5% to 64.8% [^src1][^src2].
